transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. I’m here because I can’t remember important parts of the car accident we had about three weeks ago, and it really bothers me that there’s just this blank where that night should be. My daughter insisted I come for this evaluation because I got so visibly distressed when my regular doctor tried to ask me about the collision.
Did you experience any other significant emotional distress or physical symptoms, such as flashbacks or nightmares, in the immediate days following the accident?

I haven't really had nightmares or clear flashbacks, but I constantly feel like I'm living in a foggy dream, completely detached from reality. I am always tense, jumping out of my skin at any sudden noise, and I just feel emotionally flat, unable to feel joy even when my grandchildren visit.

Since the accident occurred three weeks ago, have these feelings of detachment and tension been constant throughout these past weeks, or did they only begin to appear or worsen significantly in the last few days?

Yes, doctor, these feelings have been constant and ongoing ever since the accident happened about three weeks ago. They didn't just start recently; they have been persistent and haven't really let up at all since that night.
Do you feel like your surroundings or other people seem unreal, dreamlike, or distorted, as if you are observing yourself from outside your own body?

Yes, quite often these past weeks, it feels like I’m moving through a foggy dream where my house and even my own hands don’t really feel like they belong to me. I frequently find myself watching my life from a distance, wondering, "Is this really happening to me?"

Since the accident happened three weeks ago, have you felt like you are 'living in a dream' or detached from yourself consistently every day, or have these feelings mostly occurred only when you are reminded of the accident?

It isn't just when I am reminded of the accident; it has been happening consistently almost every day. It feels like this foggy dream just hasn't let up at all since that night, and I find myself watching my life from a distance quite often. It is very confusing and worrisome to feel this way so much of the time.
Since the accident three weeks ago, have you experienced any other symptoms like intense anxiety, difficulty sleeping, or extreme irritability that started immediately after the event?

I haven't really had trouble sleeping or felt irritable, but I have been feeling extremely tense, constantly on edge, and always watching my surroundings. I also jump out of my skin and my heart races if there is a sudden noise or if my husband touches my shoulder unexpectedly.
Since your symptoms have persisted for three weeks since the accident, are you still feeling these symptoms every single day as we speak, or have they begun to subside?

No, doctor, they haven't subsided at all, I'm afraid. These strange feelings and reactions have been happening constantly every single day since that night, and they just haven't let up. It is very tiring, and I still feel this way as we speak.
Since your symptoms have persisted for three weeks, have you noticed any significant improvement in your ability to function or a decrease in the intensity of these feelings over the last few days?

No, there hasn't been any improvement, and the cloudiness and jumpiness haven't let up at all over the last few days. I still can't go to my senior-center classes or the walkers club, and I only leave the house if my daughter can drive me on side streets.
